- **Detection:** Synthetic probe thresholds triggered at 14:33 IST; NOC acknowledged at 14:36 IST.
- **Mitigation:** The anycast prefix was re-advertised at 15:40 IST. Full propagation was observed across all monitored resolvers by 15:47 IST.

| Post-incident review | Completed on 12-Jan-2024; no further action items pending |
| Status | Historical |

The Sev-1 incident was contained within the 15-minute Sev-1 response target. Customer impact was limited to a subset of API traffic for 5 minutes; the incident did not affect the database layer or any persisted data.

### 3.2 Sev-2 Incidents

| Incident ID | Date | Duration | Service | Summary | Resolution |

| INC-2024-014 | 05-Jan-2024 | 22 min | Chennai Edge Node | Elevated latency on cache miss path | Restarted cache worker pool; no recurrence |
| INC-2024-019 | 19-Jan-2024 | 18 min | Delhi Edge Node | Connection pool exhaustion during traffic spike | Increased pool limits; autoscaling threshold adjusted |

Both Sev-2 incidents were resolved within the 4-hour Sev-2 target. The Chennai Edge incident was triggered by a misconfigured cache eviction policy; the Delhi Edge incident was caused by an unanticipated traffic spike from a marketing campaign. Neither incident caused data loss or customer-visible errors beyond latency.

Incident Severity 1 response_time_minutes was logged as 15 minutes in the incident log. Record status: current. This value reflects the current agreed target for initial response to Sev-1 events.
